ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Judy Garland

code.originalText: Ten-week review: phenobarbital taper, life after stopping the stimulant, sleep, mood, weight and work

text.paragraph: Ten-week review: phenobarbital taper, four weeks after stopping dextroamphetamine. [S]

Ms. Garland returns six weeks after her four-week review. She took the last dextroamphetamine tablet four weeks ago. For about two weeks afterwards she was tired, slept more and felt flat, and then her energy returned; she has had occasional urges to take a pill before rehearsals and has not acted on them. Her appetite has come back and she eats three meals on most days. She has gained 1.3 kg since the last visit, and she worries about it; we talked about it without a target. The step to 64.8 mg of phenobarbital went smoothly. Two weeks ago, at the sick visit for laryngitis, the next step was paused; her voice recovered within six days and she is back to singing. She sleeps about six hours on most nights. She saw the dietitian last week. Her mood is better. [S]

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Joint Clinical Practice Guideline on Benzodiazepine Tapering: Considerations When Risks Outweigh Benefits (2025); The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder (2024); Clinical Practice Guideline for the Pharmacologic Treatment of Chronic Insomnia in Adults: An American Academy of Sleep Medicine Clinical Practice Guideline (2017); Management of Chronic Insomnia Disorder in Adults: A Clinical Practice Guideline From the American College of Physicians (2016); U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, 2024 (2024); Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs (PDMPs) (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monograph (2026)
